tools.name: Helios
tools.what: 14B real-time long-video generation model: minute-scale clips at 19.5 FPS on a SINGLE H100, without KV-cache/causal-masking/sparse-attention tricks; group offloading drops VRAM to ~6 GB, multi-GPU context parallelism supported
tools.why: The reel's numbers are TRUE but the hardware claim is not. README (PKU-YuanGroup, TPAMI 2026) states plainly: 19.5 FPS end-to-end on a single H100, ~10 FPS on one Ascend NPU; a user on better hardware hit 20.89 FPS. So 'standard hardware' means a data-centre GPU, not a gaming card. The genuinely useful part for us is group offloading: ~6 GB VRAM inference for a 14B video model, plus training batching that fits four 14B models in 80 GB. api.github.com: 2279 stars / 204 forks, Apache-2.0, created 2026-03-02, pushed 2026-11-01 - a real maintained research repo with a live HF Space. Reel hygiene: gitfinds.si, 39 likes but 17 comments, CTA is 'comment HELI and I will DM the link' and the caption never names the repo - the name had to be recovered from the audio track ('the repo is called Helios'). Verdict watch, not use: this box has no GPU, and renting an H100 to generate clips we cannot cut at 20 fps is a cost with no revenue attached yet. It becomes the right tool the day the rig exists or a H100 hour is cheaper than a stock-footage subscription.

tools.name: Codevember 2026

tools.name: Latent Library

tools.why: Verified on api.github.com and the repo's own README/LICENSE, 2026-11-23. Real project, small: 96 stars / 6 forks, created 2026-02-09, last push 2026-08-24 (three months untouched), Java 545k + Vue 224k lines. Release v1.2.2 ships a portable Windows .exe 228.5 MB (89 downloads), Linux AppImage 272.4 MB (47), macOS arm64 dmg 293.2 MB (15) - self-contained Java 21, no installer, no system Java. Tagging is a bundled WD14 ONNX model (~300 MB) on CPU, no GPU needed. Licence is MIT with the Commons Clause: free to use/modify/share, but reselling it or hosting it as a paid service is not allowed. The whole point of the tool is reading the generation parameters buried in PNG/EXIF from ComfyUI and Automatic1111, plus duplicate detection and smart collections over that metadata. Reel (github_dev, 2026-11-21, 37 s, 62 likes / 1 comment) is a README scroll with a voice-over paraphrasing the caption - zero footage of the app actually running, and the app screenshots in it are the README's own stills; a low-res read of the address bar invented the owner 'emrahcelebi' (404), the real repo is erroralex/Latent-Library. tools.name: rVPN
tools.what: Stealth VPN protocol in Rust: TLS 1.3 + WebSocket transport, X3DH + Double Ratchet, pooled multiplexing, decoy website behind the endpoint
tools.why: Checked 2026-11-11 after Ahmad's link to rvpn.org. Real and open: 75,236 lines of Rust across 6 crates (core/client/server/mobile/split-tunnel/tls), AGPLv3 (dual-licensed), 442 locked deps, release v1.3.6 with signed-ecosystem binaries — I downloaded rvpn-x86_64-linux-gnu and its sha256 matched. Server runs (plain-WS mode for a reverse proxy) on a local port; the client needs a real TLS cert, so a full tunnel test needs a domain. MEASURED CLAIM CHECK: captured the ClientHello of the client with --fingerprint chrome, firefox and none set, with SNI configured — all three send the IDENTICAL hello (JA3 ae182ac85a70abc053529488dd3d3a1c, 3 TLS1.3 ciphers, 7 extensions: SNI/groups/ALPN/sigalgs/key_share/psk_modes/supported_versions), while real Chrome 145 sends 15 ciphers and 16 extensions (JA3 2bcd7848d91e9a7908f369fe6a8dbf91, GREASE, ECH). So 'looks exactly like Chrome/Firefox' does not hold at the hello in v1.3.6 — the flag changes nothing on this path. It is still ordinary TLS 1.3 on :443 with a real SNI and a decoy site (that part is true and useful), but the fingerprint is distinctive and Iran's DPI can match it. Marketing also says 'git checkout v1.4.0' while the newest tag is v1.3.6, and the site's sha256/0xA13F signature lines are decoration until verified per-release. Verdict: a legitimately interesting protocol to experiment with (self-host a node behind Caddy with a real domain), not the 'indistinguishable' drop-in the page sells. Artifacts: workspace/rvpn-test.

tools.name: Edge0 (edge0-infer)
tools.what: Streaming MoE inference engine: 35B-A3B (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 4-bit) with expert weights on SSD, a trained prerouter and Recover-LoRA
tools.why: Ran it for real on 2026-11-11, not just read the page. Reel link -> repo (9,689 stars, Apache-2.0, C++, arXiv 2609.18063, weights on HF, 19.7 GB source + 22 GB converted). NoLinux preset exists, but the generic `cmake --preset cpu` builds on Ubuntu with two local changes only: drop -Werror in cmake/MoeTargets.cmake (gcc 15 promotes warnings clang did not) and -DMOE_BUILD_TESTS=OFF (a test file misses <algorithm>). Deployed on the ki box (i5-10500T, 6c/12t, 32 GB, SATA/NVMe SSD, no GPU), 12-core build. MEASURED: 6.07 decode tok/s, 6.39 s to first token, 68 tokens in 11.2 s, peak RSS 3.09 GB (matches their 2.9-3.4 GB claim), decode read 12.67 GB from SSD for those 68 tokens with a 42.3% expert-cache hit rate (prerouter: 8,976 prefetches, only 67 late). Quality: coherent two-sentence answers in English and Persian on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. So the headline is TRUE: a 35B MoE really runs in ~3 GB of RAM on a 6-core office CPU; the cost is 6 tok/s (their Windows i5-12400 reference is 7.3-8.2). Use it for local experiments and for the '35B in 3 GB' video with our own numbers; not for interactive chat or anything latency-sensitive. Published as a short on ALGORHYTHM 2026-11-11: https://youtube.com/shorts/0YF6DU4SJsk (English, 40 s, cards carry our measured numbers).

tools.name: prompts.chat
tools.what: Open prompt + agent-skill library (2,916 prompts incl. 650 image and 89 video, 177 multi-file agent skills) with a stateless MCP endpoint and a Claude Code plugin
tools.why: Verified 2026-11-11 by hand, not from the reel. GitHub f/prompts.chat: 176,920 stars, created 2022-12-05, pushed same day; licence is dual - MIT for code, CC0 for the prompt content, so prompts are commercially usable (GitHub metadata says NOASSERTION, read LICENSE). REST /api/prompts?perPage=1 gives total 2,916 (TEXT 1,906 / IMAGE 650 / VIDEO 89 / AUDIO 4); the site showed 177 skills and 47 workflows. The Persian reel (saeedkhorsandi0, 2026-11-10) claims '10,000+ prompts' - that is inflated ~3.4x and the 'comment LIBRARY' funnel never delivered a link (10 comments, all the word 'library', no reply, no pinned comment); the link is just the free site. MCP is real and needs no key: POST https://prompts.chat/api/mcp answers stateless JSON-RPC with 17 tools (search_prompts, get_prompt, search_skills, get_skill, save_*, bots/teams); get_skill returns every file of a skill. Local stdio: npx -y @fkadev/prompts.chat-mcp 1.0.9. Catch: both search_prompts and REST q AND every word, so multi-word queries return 0 - our CLI splits and merges. prompts/list caps at ~420 entries, so it is not the catalogue. Skill-library keyword search is noisy (youtube/thumbnail/hook return dev skills); the prompt catalogue is the part worth using. Wired: workspace/prompts-cli/pmcp.py (search/get/count/skills/skill --install), skill prompts-chat v2 with references/mcp.md, and mcp_servers.prompts-chat in config. First real use: cloned srt-subtitle-quality-checker (6 files) and ran its stdlib checker on our own ep01 SRT - 120 cues, 0 HIGH, 115 WARN, all line-length above 42 chars, i.e. a real gate for the burned-in captions.

tools.name: colibri
tools.what: C engine that streams MoE expert weights from NVMe, so 300B-1.5T models (GLM-5.2 744B, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3) run on CPU-only machines; OpenAI/Anthropic API, dashboard, MCP server
tools.why: Installed and measured on the ki home box 2026-11-12 (Ubuntu 26.04.1, i5-10500T 6C/12T, 30 GB RAM, SSD, no GPU), not just read: make -C c portable built with gcc 15.2 in seconds, the per-family engine with ARCH=native, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (int4, 23 GB) served on 127.0.0.1:8000/v1. MEASURED via the OpenAI API at temperature 0, three prompts: TTFT 0.53-0.77 s, decode 11.46-11.57 tok/s, end-to-end 9.8-10.9 tok/s, 586-652 tokens/min, prefill 43-60 tok/s, RSS 14.5-14.9 GB, MemAvailable 16.3->15.5 GB, disk reads only 54 MB short / 156 MB long because the model is resident. That is 1.9x the vendor's 6.0 tok/s CPU figure for the same model, thanks to 12 threads and a 30 GB RAM cache. Fit on this box (the tool's own setup --list, 32.8 GB seen, 753 GB free): glm-5.2 (744B, 429 GB) is 'good' because only 9.9 GB must stay in RAM; deepseek-v4-flash 167 GB and mimo-v2.6-flash 172 GB fit; kimi-k3 (1.5 T) needs 1594 GB disk and does not. The reel's claim (744B on an ordinary PC, no expensive GPU) is therefore TRUE, with the honest cost: vendor numbers are 0.05-0.1 tok/s on a 25 GB laptop, 1.83 tok/s CPU-only on 128 GB. GLM-5.2 download (429 GB) started on the same box at a measured 38.5 MB/s; its benchmark is appended to docs/reports/colibri-ki-2026-11-12.pdf when it lands. Report + raw data: docs/reports/colibri-ki-2026-11-12.pdf / .md, data/colibri-ki.json. Skill: devops/colibri-local-moe. Install: clone, make -C c portable -j$(nproc), python3 c/coli setup --list, setup --model qwen36-35b --yes.

tools.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
tools.what: Topic or keyword in, finished 9:16 video out: LLM script -> footage search keywords -> stock clips -> subtitles -> BGM -> render. WebUI plus HTTP API; provider-agnostic (many LLM keys, Pexels/Pixabay/Coverr or local material for footage).
tools.verdict_note: Checked 2026-11-18 by cloning it (341 MB, 359 py files, deps: moviepy 2.2.1, streamlit, faster-whisper, edge-tts, openai). Verified on api.github.com: 144,268 stars, MIT, created 2024-03-11, pushed 2026-11-18, not archived. NOT adopted as our engine, and the reason is measured, not aesthetic: it produces stock-footage explainers, and our channel's own retention data says the format that holds viewers is a made-up-looking claim proven by motion (35 s clip 53 % retention, 1038 views), not a stock-clip montage. Volume was never our bottleneck - topic consistency and retention were. It needs one free key we do not have (Pexels/Pixabay) OR video_source='local' with our own clips. Its 29 bundled mp3 beds under resource/songs are NOT usable: the repo is MIT for CODE, the audio provenance is unstated, so lifting them into monetised videos is a copyright risk. BEST POSITION: content. It is a strong dev-lane story (144k stars, one-keyword-to-video) and the cards for that short are built at team/formats/demo-moneyprinter/.

tools.name: MiniMax H3 integrations
tools.what: Community index for MiniMax H3, a video model that generates up to 15 s clips at up to 2K with NATIVE stereo audio. Two variants: FL2VA (0-2 keyframe images) and Ref2VA (up to 9 images, 3 clips of 2-15 s, 3 audio clips, 12 files total). Lists checkpoints down to NF4 that run from 8 GB VRAM via DiffSynth-Studio, plus Apple-Silicon engines (h3.c, Draw Things, mlx-serve).
tools.verdict_note: Checked 2026-11-18 after Ahmad's reel (115 likes). api.github.com: the index repo has 580 stars, created 2026-11-12; the model repo MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3 has 12,008 stars, pushed 2026-10-28, and NO declared licence (license: None) - so redistributing generated output is a legal unknown until the model card states terms. Hardware: 8 GB VRAM minimum for the NF4 path, which this box does not have (no GPU at all). NOT usable as our production engine today; it is a 'the format is coming' signal, and a strong dev-lane story for ALGORHYTHM the moment someone rents a GPU.

tools.name: InferSSD
tools.what: Streams MoE experts from SSD so models far larger than RAM/VRAM run on ordinary machines. Built on llama.cpp, standard GGUF, browser chat + OpenAI-compatible API. Runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (763B total), Muse-Spark-Open (816B), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma4 E4B.
tools.verdict_note: Checked 2026-11-19 after Ahmad's reel (@reporadarai, README-scroll format). api.github.com: 1,235 stars, Apache-2.0, created 2026-10-22, pushed 2026-11-19 - alive and shipping. It is a DIRECT competitor to colibri (which we already shipped a short about) and benchmarks itself against it. Every published hardware row is a GPU box or an M5 Max: RTX 5060 Ti 8+16 GB, RTX 5090 32+32 GB, DGX Spark 128 GB, MacBook 48-128 GB. Our box is 6 cores / 7 GB / no GPU, below every row, so the 164.5 tok/s headline is not reachable here and the 763B model is out of reach by an order of magnitude. BEST POSITION: content, not our stack - 'two engines, one SSD' head-to-head against colibri is a genuinely strong ALGORHYTHM short, and we have first-hand numbers for one side of that comparison.

tools.name: Claude Blender Skills
tools.what: MIT pack of 3 Blender film-production workflows (night FPV drone shot, forest scene, snowy-night short) with real Blender-Python scripts and a 127.0.0.1:9876 bridge an LLM drives
tools.why: Real, not a stub: 150 stars / 32 forks, created and last pushed 2026-10-25 (never updated), 2.3 MB of genuine production code. The standout is motion-driven sound: 11_motion_data.py dumps per-frame camera/drone/car telemetry, 12_build_sfx.py applies doppler = 343/(343+radial), gain = 1/distance, air absorption and scene pan, with throttle-driven RPM. Reel overstates one detail: the pitch shift of passing cars is a recorded sample placed at closest approach, not computed. Constraints: Blender 4.4+, author rendered on one RTX 5070 12GB, scripts hardcoded to his scene names. Saved 2026-11-20 at /opt/data/workspace/blender-skills; only the CPU-only SFX scripts (numpy/scipy/ffmpeg) are usable on this GPU-less box.

tools.name: AI Video Factory
tools.what: Topic to finished, narrated 1080p YouTube episode: Claude/ACP agents write the script and shot plan and draw vector art, Remotion renders, and the run also emits .srt, title/description/chapters/tags, a 1280x720 thumbnail and a 1080x1920 Short
tools.why: Verified by running it here, not by the reel. Clone 27 MB, v0.6.8 (397ccba, release 2026-11-22), MIT, TypeScript+Remotion, 590 stars / 81 forks, created 2026-10-29 so 25 days old at check. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 12.7 s (pnpm 11.25 auto-selected from packageManager, node_modules 1.4 GB). The documented no-credentials demo works on this CPU-only 6-core 7.8 GB box: STORE=fs LEDGER=jsonl YS_RENDER_GL=swangle render-demo built a synthetic 3-shot tr episode, paused at the preview approval gate, and approve + run --only render/package/short produced 1920x1080 30 fps 9.8 s 5.68 MB H.264+AAC, a 304 B srt, a 1280x720 JPEG thumbnail and a 1080x1920 3.97 MB Short in ~2.5 min total (~0.26 s/frame, 294 frames in 75 s; first run downloads Remotion's 98.9 MB Chrome Headless Shell). The repo's own video audit ran at every export: 0 findings. Agent cost $0.0000, zero paid calls. 64 style packs is TRUE: STYLE_PACKS in packages/core/src/styles.ts holds exactly 64 ids (ukiyo-e, risograph, blueprint, technical-cutaway, paper-quilling...); ACP support for Antigravity/agy is real code (packages/agents/src/acp.ts), not a logo strip. Blocker, exactly: the generation stages need FAL_KEY or GEMINI_API_KEY + an ELEVENLABS_API_KEY for narration and a Claude Code login/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an ACP agent; this box holds only OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so the demo proves the renderer and the packaging, not the art (its keyframes are FFmpeg test patterns - SMPTE-ish bars, plasma, TV static). Languages: narration any language the voice provider supports (Persian possible), Studio UI tr/en only. Reel hygiene: the 28 s gittrend.io promo never shows the product (9 frames = same README scrolled), its CTA is a comment-for-link funnel, and it shows the 0.6.0 banner while the repo is at 0.6.8; a low-res read of the address bar invented the owner 'yusufcaner' (404) - the real owner, ersinkoc, is only legible at 2x. Verdict consider, not use: nothing of ours calls it yet. Ahead of our stack on approval gates, cost ledger with per-episode cap, automatic video audit at every export, art direction as 64 data packs, and --only short producing the 9:16 cut without a second edit; behind it on zero-key operation, Persian, and per-frame control.
